_comment: SPA history fallback for the admin console — CloudFront E31NGXQN85PXV7,
origin S3 shramsafal-admin-prod, public at https://admin.shramsafal.in.
spec: admin-v3-migration (Task 28 Step 1, register row A44)
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS AT ALL
admin-web is a client-side router. There is no object in S3 at the key
'farms', 'farmer-health/<farmId>' or 'ops/errors'. Every one of those
paths works in `vite dev` — the dev server rewrites unknown paths to
index.html — and every one of them 404s in production unless the CDN does
the same thing. That is the ONE failure mode of this whole migration that
is invisible until deployment: the app is correct, the tests are green,
the build is green, and every shareable URL the plan just built is dead.
The rewrite has therefore existed as a CloudFront custom-error-response —
but ONLY in the AWS console, typed by hand, recorded nowhere. Recreate the
distribution and every deep link dies silently, with nothing in the repo
to say what was lost. It is committed here so that cannot happen.
🛑 THE COROLLARY, WHICH IS THE HALF THAT CATCHES PEOPLE
With 403/404 mapped to /index.html at status 200, ANY MISSING OBJECT ON
THIS DISTRIBUTION RETURNS HTTP 200 WITH Content-Type: text/html.
- a missing JS bundle returns 200
- a typo'd asset path returns 200
- a completely failed deploy returns 200 on every URL you try
So a status-code-only smoke check produces FALSE GREENS here. Every prod
proof — in scripts/deploy-s3.sh, in a runbook, in a PR comment — must
assert Content-Type, not just status. If an asset comes back text/html it
does not exist and you are looking at the fallback wearing its clothes.
WHY 403 AND NOT ONLY 404
An S3 REST origin behind OAC returns 403 AccessDenied, not 404 NoSuchKey,
for a key that is absent whenever the bucket policy does not grant
s3:ListBucket. Mapping only 404 leaves every deep link 403ing, which looks
like a permissions bug on an admin console and is the worst possible
misreading. Both are mapped.
WHY ErrorCachingMinTTL IS 0
CloudFront's default is 10s and the console will happily let you set 300.
Any non-zero value caches the FALLBACK for a path — so an asset that is
missing because a deploy was mid-flight keeps serving index.html at the
edge for that long after the file lands. Correctness beats a cache hit on
an error path.
HONESTY NOTE — THIS FILE HAS NOT BEEN DIFFED AGAINST THE LIVE
DISTRIBUTION. It was authored from the behaviour the console depends on,
not read back from AWS: prod compute is hibernated and no AWS call was
made while writing it. It is the INTENDED state. scripts/deploy-s3.sh
--check-spa-fallback compares it against the live distribution and prints
the difference; run that before trusting this file as a record of what is
deployed.
CHECK (read-only, safe):
aws cloudfront get-distribution-config --id E31NGXQN85PXV7 \
--query 'DistributionConfig.CustomErrorResponses'
or: src/clients/admin-web/scripts/deploy-s3.sh --check-spa-fallback
APPLY (founder only — CloudFront has no partial update; you must send the
WHOLE DistributionConfig back with its ETag, so this fragment is merged
rather than posted):
aws cloudfront get-distribution-config --id E31NGXQN85PXV7 > /tmp/dc.json
jq --slurpfile f aws/admin/cloudfront-spa-fallback.json \
'.DistributionConfig.CustomErrorResponses = ($f[0] | del(._comment))' \
/tmp/dc.json > /tmp/merged.json
aws cloudfront update-distribution --id E31NGXQN85PXV7 \
--if-match "$(jq -r .ETag /tmp/dc.json)" \
--distribution-config "file:///tmp/merged.json"   # .DistributionConfig only
or: src/clients/admin-web/scripts/deploy-s3.sh --apply-spa-fallback
ROLLBACK: same merge with CustomErrorResponses set to {"Quantity":0}.
That restores real 403/404s — and kills every deep link. It is only ever
the right move if this console stops being a client-side router.
